screens.name: minervini_trend_template
screens.title: Stage 2 Uptrend
screens.description: The eight-point filter for a stock in a confirmed Stage 2 advance: price above the 50, 150 and 200-day averages, the 150 above the 200, the 200 itself rising, price well off its 52-week low and close to its high, and relative strength in the top third of the market.
screens.origin: Mark Minervini's Trend Template
screens.why: Minervini's argument is that almost all large winners spend their advance above these averages, so the template is a filter for where to look rather than a trigger. It removes basing and declining stocks before any pattern work begins.
screens.manage: Conventionally used as a universe filter, not an entry. Traders then wait for a tight consolidation and buy the breakout from it.
screens.expr: adj_close > sma_50 and adj_close > sma_150 and adj_close > sma_200 and sma_50 > sma_150 and sma_150 > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and pct_from_52w_low > 30 and pct_from_52w_high > -25 and rs_rank >= 70

screens.name: vcp_squeeze
screens.title: Volatility Contraction
screens.description: Three consecutive ten-session ranges, each tighter than the one before, the last of them under eight percent wide, with volume drying up and price holding a shallow base near its highs.
screens.origin: Minervini's VCP, via the tightening-base idea in O'Neil's work
screens.why: Contracting range with falling volume says supply is being exhausted: sellers who wanted out are out. The sequence is the pattern - Minervini's point is that each pullback must be shallower than the last. A single "tighter now than before" ratio is not the same test and passes whenever the earlier window happened to be wide.
screens.manage: The conventional entry is the break of the base's high on expanding volume; the stop sits under the final, tightest contraction.
screens.expr: adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and contract_seq == 1 and contract_ratio < 0.7 and tightness < 8 and vol_dryup < 0.9 and base_depth > -12 and rs_rank >= 60

screens.name: ema21_pullback
screens.title: Pullback to the 21 EMA
screens.description: An established uptrend where price has come back to the 21-day EMA rather than breaking down: still above the 50-day, still above the 200-day, RSI cooled but not broken.
screens.origin: The trend-continuation pullback, the most widely taught swing setup
screens.why: A trend rarely runs without pausing. Buying the pause rather than the breakout gives a tighter stop, which is where most of the edge in this setup actually lives - the risk is small, not the win rate large.
screens.manage: Usually entered on a reversal candle at the average, with the stop under the pullback low. If price closes below the 50-day the premise is gone.
screens.expr: adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and dist_ema_21 > -4 and dist_ema_21 < 1.5 and ext_ema21_15 >= 5 and off_high_10 < -2 and rsi_14 > 40 and rsi_14 < 62 and ret_60d > 8

screens.name: high_tight_breakout
screens.title: Breakout at 52-Week High
screens.description: Price is within three percent of its 52-week high, breaking out on volume at least one and a half times its twenty-day average.
screens.origin: Darvas boxes, and O'Neil's new-high buying
screens.why: A stock at a new high has no overhead supply: nobody above is waiting to get out at break-even. Darvas traded almost nothing else. The volume condition separates a real breakout from a drift.
screens.manage: Typically bought on the breakout day or the first tight day after it, with the stop below the box that was broken.
screens.expr: adj_close > hi_250_prior and vol_ratio > 1.5 and ret_1d > 1 and adj_close > sma_50 and rs_rank >= 60

screens.name: inside_bar_coil
screens.title: Inside-Bar Coil
screens.description: Today's entire range sits inside yesterday's, in a stock that is trending and already tight.
screens.origin: The NR7 / inside-bar squeeze
screens.why: An inside bar is a one-day standoff: neither side could extend the range. After a run, it usually resolves in the direction of the trend, and it gives an unusually well-defined stop.
screens.manage: Entry on a break of the inside bar's high, stop under its low. Small risk per trade is the whole point; it fails often and cheaply.
screens.expr: inside_bar == 1 and adj_close > sma_20 and sma_20 > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and atr_pct < 5 and rs_rank >= 50

screens.name: close_above_monthly_tc
screens.title: Above Monthly TC
screens.description: Close reclaims the top of last month's Central Pivot Range, with the 50-day average beneath it.
screens.origin: Central Pivot Range, floor-trader pivots
screens.why: The CPR summarises last month into three lines. Trading above the top one means the month opened on the bullish side of its own prior value area, which is the bias most CPR traders start from.
screens.manage: Usually held while price stays above the monthly TC; a close back inside the range ends the premise.
screens.expr: adj_close > m_cpr_tc and adj_close > sma_50

screens.name: narrow_cpr_breakout
screens.title: Narrow CPR Breakout
screens.description: Last month's Central Pivot Range was unusually narrow and price is now trading above it, with the 200-day beneath.
screens.origin: Narrow-CPR expansion
screens.why: A narrow CPR means last month closed near its own average - agreement, little trend. Ranges that tight tend to be followed by expansion, and the direction of the break is the tell.
screens.manage: Traded as a breakout: entry above TC, invalidated on a close back below BC.
screens.expr: m_cpr_width < 2.0 and m_cpr_width_rank < 0.34 and adj_close > m_cpr_tc and since_m_cpr_tc_cross <= 5 and adj_close > sma_200

screens.name: weekly_tc_reclaim
screens.title: Weekly TC Reclaim
screens.description: Close above last week's CPR top, with the 20-day average rising beneath it and the week so far positive.
screens.origin: Weekly CPR
screens.why: A shorter-horizon version of the monthly rule, for traders who work the week rather than the month.
screens.manage: Held while above the weekly TC; reassessed each Monday when the level moves.
screens.expr: adj_close > w_cpr_tc and since_w_cpr_tc_cross <= 3 and adj_close > sma_20 and ret_5d > 0

screens.name: volume_shocker
screens.title: Volume Shockers
screens.description: Volume at more than three times its twenty-day average on an up day, with price above the 20-day.
screens.origin: Unusual-volume scanning
screens.why: Volume is the one input that cannot be drawn on a chart after the fact. A three-fold day means participation changed, which either confirms a move or front-runs news. It is a prompt to look, not a setup on its own.
screens.manage: Most traders wait for the day after: a hold of the spike's range is constructive, an immediate give-back is not.
screens.expr: vol_ratio > 3 and ret_1d > 2 and adj_close > sma_20

screens.name: momentum_leaders
screens.title: Momentum Leaders
screens.description: Strong over one, three and six months at once, with the 50-day above the 200-day.
screens.origin: Cross-sectional momentum, the most replicated anomaly in the literature
screens.why: Relative momentum persists over three to twelve-month horizons across almost every market studied. Requiring several windows at once filters out a single lucky month.
screens.manage: Usually held on a rebalance schedule rather than a stop, and exited when the name drops out of the leadership group.
screens.expr: mom_12_1 > 15 and ret_60d > 12 and ret_120d > 15 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200

screens.name: oversold_in_uptrend
screens.title: Oversold in Uptrend
screens.description: RSI below 35 while price still holds above the 200-day average and the six-month return is positive.
screens.origin: RSI mean reversion inside a trend
screens.why: Mean reversion works far better inside an uptrend than against one. The 200-day condition is what separates a pullback from a breakdown; without it this screen simply finds falling stocks.
screens.manage: Short leash. The premise is a bounce, so it is usually abandoned quickly if one does not come.
screens.expr: rsi_14 < 35 and adj_close > sma_200 and ret_120d > 0

screens.name: trend_stack
screens.title: Full Trend Stack
screens.description: Price above the 20, the 20 above the 50, the 50 above the 200, with RSI not yet stretched.
screens.origin: Moving-average ribbon alignment
screens.why: Every timeframe pointing the same way. A coarse but honest health check rather than a trigger - it tells you the trend is intact, not that now is the moment.
screens.manage: Used as a backdrop filter for other setups more often than traded directly.
screens.expr: adj_close > sma_20 and sma_20 > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and rsi_14 < 70

screens.name: monthly_r1_breakout
screens.title: Monthly R1 Breakout
screens.description: Price has closed above last month's first resistance pivot within the last three sessions, on volume above its twenty-day average, with the 50-day average beneath.
screens.origin: Floor-trader pivots, monthly timeframe
screens.why: R1 is the level the month's own range projects as the first place supply should appear. Clearing it says the projection was wrong on the low side - the month is trading beyond what last month's range accounted for. On the monthly timeframe there is only one such crossing per leg, which is what makes it worth watching rather than a number price wanders across.
screens.manage: Conventionally entered on the close above R1 or the first tight day after it, stop back under R1, with monthly R2 as the mechanical first target.
screens.expr: adj_close > m_r1 and since_m_r1_cross <= 3 and vol_ratio > 1.3 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200

screens.name: monthly_r1_retest
screens.title: Monthly R1 Retest
screens.description: Price broke above last month's R1 in the past two to fifteen sessions, has come back to touch it within one percent, and is still closing above it.
screens.origin: Broken-resistance-becomes-support, on the monthly pivot
screens.why: The retest is the part of a pivot break that carries the risk definition. Buying the break means guessing; waiting for price to return to the level and hold turns R1 into a floor you can put a stop under, and gives a losing trade a small, immediate answer rather than a slow one.
screens.manage: Entry on the hold of the level, stop a little under it. A close back below R1 ends the premise outright - that is the breakdown point for this setup.
screens.expr: dist_m_r1 > 0 and low3_dist_m_r1 < 1.0 and low3_dist_m_r1 > -2.5 and since_m_r1_cross >= 2 and since_m_r1_cross <= 15 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200

screens.name: pocket_pivot
screens.title: Pocket Pivot
screens.description: An up day whose volume is larger than every DOWN day's volume in the prior ten sessions, inside a shallow base in an uptrend.
screens.origin: Gil Morales and Chris Kacher, "Trade Like an O'Neil Disciple"
screens.why: Comparing today's buying against the last ten days of SELLING is the whole idea. It is a way to see institutional accumulation starting inside a base, before the breakout that everyone else is waiting for, which is why it tends to fire earlier and at lower risk than a new-high buy.
screens.manage: Bought on the pivot day itself, stop under the base's low or the 50-day average, whichever is tighter. It fails when the base fails.
screens.expr: pocket_pivot == 1 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and base_depth > -15 and dist_sma_10 < 5 and dist_sma_10 > -5 and rs_rank >= 50

screens.name: donchian_breakout
screens.title: 20-Day Donchian Breakout
screens.description: Today's close is above the highest close of the prior twenty sessions, in a stock already above its long averages and with enough daily range to move.
screens.origin: The Turtle system's entry channel; Donchian's original rule
screens.why: This is the most-tested breakout rule in existence and the one least dependent on interpretation - there is no pattern to see, only a number to exceed. Its edge has always come from a small number of very large trends, not from hit rate, and it should be read that way.
screens.manage: The Turtles exited on a ten-day low and sized by ATR. Both matter more than the entry; without a trailing exit this rule has no system around it.
screens.expr: adj_close > hi_20_prior and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and vol_ratio > 1.2 and atr_pct > 1.5 and rs_rank >= 50

screens.name: three_weeks_tight
screens.title: Three Weeks Tight
screens.description: Three weeks of closes within two and a half percent of each other, near the highs, in a leading stock.
screens.horizon: Swing - entry on the break, days
screens.origin: Minervini and O'Neil's "3 weeks tight" continuation pattern
screens.why: After an advance, three weeks of going nowhere with no give-back is a refusal to sell. The pattern is prized because the stop is absurdly tight - the entire risk is the width of the tightness itself.
screens.manage: Bought above the high of the tight range. A close below the range's low is the breakdown point and is usually a small loss by construction.
screens.expr: tight_3w_pct < 1.5 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and pct_from_52w_high > -15 and rs_rank >= 60

screens.name: stage2_base_breakout
screens.title: Stage 2 Base Breakout
screens.description: Price clears the highest close of the last sixty sessions - roughly a quarter's worth of base - on volume half again its average, above a rising 200-day average.
screens.origin: Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis, 30-week moving average
screens.why: Weinstein's argument is that a stock moves through four stages and that only Stage 2 is worth owning. The breakout from a long base above a rising 30-week average is his definition of that transition, and the volume condition is what distinguishes it from drift.
screens.manage: Held for the stage, not the swing; the conventional exit is a close below the 30-week average or a break of the breakout level on volume.
screens.expr: adj_close > hi_60_prior and adj_close > sma_150 and sma_150_slope > 0 and adj_close > sma_200 and vol_ratio > 1.5 and rs_rank >= 60

screens.name: episodic_pivot
screens.title: Episodic Pivot
screens.description: A gap up of more than four percent on at least four times average volume, closing in the upper part of the day's range.
screens.origin: Pradeep Bonde (Stockbee); the "surprise" gap
screens.why: An episodic pivot is a gap that is caused by something - a result, an order, a change of story - rather than by drift. The gap is the signature of information arriving overnight, and the close near the high says the market spent the whole session refusing to give it back.
screens.manage: A watchlist signal, not a buy-the-open signal. The gap day's LOW is the structure this setup gives you - everyone who bought the news is above it - so that is the stop, and filling the gap means the premise is wrong. Measured over 343 signals, three entries with that same stop and a 2R target: buying the next open returns +0.195R per signal with 7.5% risk; WAITING for a pullback to the gap day's close returns +0.346R with 6.7% risk and still fills 88% of the time. Waiting for a break of the gap day's HIGH is the worst of the three at +0.145R - it only sets up 62% of the time and buying the high against a stop at the low makes R an 11.5% monster. The lesson is to enter nearer the stop, not to wait for more confirmation.
screens.expr: gap_pct > 4 and vol_ratio > 4 and close_pos > 0.6 and adj_close > sma_50

screens.name: rsi2_reversion
screens.title: RSI(2) Snapback
screens.description: A two-period RSI below eight in a stock still above both its 50 and 200-day averages.
screens.origin: Larry Connors' short-term mean reversion research
screens.why: RSI(2) is built to saturate. Connors' finding was that in an established uptrend, the extreme readings mark short-lived exhaustion rather than damage, and that the shorter the lookback the cleaner the effect. The trend filters are not optional - without them this buys falling knives.
screens.manage: Explicitly a short hold. The published rule exits on a close above the 5-day average rather than on a target or a stop.
screens.expr: rsi_2 < 8 and adj_close > sma_200 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_200_slope > 0 and ret_120d > 0

screens.name: r1_breakout_retest
screens.title: R1 Breakout, Then Retest
screens.description: Price cleared last month's R1 on volume above its own 21-day average within the last two to fifteen sessions, and has now pulled back to touch either that R1 level or the 9 EMA, still closing above both.
screens.horizon: Swing - entry on the hold, days
screens.origin: Pivot breakout with volume confirmation, entered on the pullback
screens.why: Two separate things have to be true, and the order matters. The breakout is only worth anything if volume showed up on the day it happened - a drift across a pivot on average volume is not supply changing hands. And the breakout itself is a poor entry: it is the widest point from any sensible stop. The pullback is where the trade becomes definable, because price returns to a level you can put a stop under. Which pullback depends on how strong the move was. A merely decent breakout hands R1 back and retests it. A strong one never does - it pulls in to the 9 EMA instead and turns from there. Requiring only the first would discard the better half of the setups, so either qualifies.
screens.manage: Entry on the hold of whichever level was touched, stop a little under it. A close back below R1 ends the premise - that level is what the whole setup was built on. Measured on the sibling Episodic Pivot screen, entering near the stop on a pullback roughly doubled expectancy against buying the breakout day, which is the same reasoning applied here.
screens.expr: since_r1_vol_breakout >= 2 and since_r1_vol_breakout <= 15 and adj_close > m_r1 and adj_close > ema_9 and ( (low3_dist_m_r1 < 1.0 and low3_dist_m_r1 > -2.5) or (low3_dist_ema_9 < 1.0 and low3_dist_ema_9 > -2.5) ) and sma_50 > sma_200

screens.name: spring_reclaim
screens.title: Shakeout Reclaim
screens.description: Price broke below its twenty-day low - where the obvious stops sit - and closed back above that low the same session, in the upper half of the day's range, inside a longer uptrend.
screens.horizon: Swing - entry within days of the reclaim
screens.origin: Wyckoff's spring; Linda Raschke's Turtle Soup
screens.why: The stop run is the setup, not the hazard. A break of an obvious low pulls in breakout sellers and triggers resting stops; when the session closes back above that low, every one of those sellers is offside and the supply underneath has been spent in public. The low it happened on is a floor that has been TESTED rather than assumed, which is exactly what an ordinary support level is not.
screens.manage: Entry on the reclaim or the first day that holds above it. Stop under the shakeout low - and this screen requires that low to sit at least 1.5 ATR away, so routine noise cannot reach it. If it goes, the absorption failed and the premise is gone.
screens.expr: since_spring <= 3 and adj_close > lo_20_prior and atr_to_spring >= 1.5 and adj_close > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and ud_vol_20 > 1.0 and rs_rank >= 45

screens.name: held_breakout
screens.title: Breakout That Held
screens.description: Price cleared its sixty-day high three to fifteen sessions ago on volume above its own average, and since that day the lowest low has never returned to the breakout level - nobody who bought the break has been stopped out.
screens.origin: Breakout confirmation by time rather than by price
screens.why: A failed breakout announces itself quickly: it gives the level back within a session or three. Rather than guess in advance which break is real, this waits and checks. The lowest low since the cross is the entire test, and it is a fact rather than a forecast. The cost is obvious and worth stating: you buy higher than the breakout buyer did. What you get for it is a setup where the invalidation level has already been defended, and a stop under it that the market has shown it does not want to visit.
screens.manage: Stop under the breakout level itself, which by construction has held since the break. A close back below it means the confirmation was wrong, which is a cheap and quick answer.
screens.expr: since_brk_60 >= 3 and since_brk_60 <= 15 and brk_cushion > 0 and closes_above_brk >= 3 and brk_vol > 1.0 and adj_close > brk_level and sma_50 > sma_200 and rs_rank >= 55

screens.name: accumulation_thrust
screens.title: Quiet Accumulation
screens.description: Over the last twenty sessions, volume on up days outweighed volume on down days by more than half again, price is holding its highs with closes in the upper part of each day's range, and the range is contracting.
screens.origin: O'Neil's up/down volume ratio; volume asymmetry over a spike
screens.why: A single huge volume day is news, and news reverses. Twenty sessions of buyers consistently outweighing sellers is a position being built, and a position being built does not unwind because a level got poked. The contracting range says the buying is being done without chasing, which is what institutional accumulation looks like from the outside.
screens.manage: There is no single trigger bar here, so no single stop. Conventionally used as the filter you apply BEFORE taking any breakout or pullback entry in the name - the ratio dropping below 1 is what ends it.
screens.expr: ud_vol_20 > 1.5 and close_pos_3 > 0.55 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and base_depth > -10 and atr_ratio_60 < 1.0 and rs_rank >= 60

screens.name: near_52w_high
screens.title: Holding the 52-Week High
screens.description: Price sits within twelve percent of its fifty-two week high, above a rising set of averages, with relative strength in the top fifth of the market.
screens.origin: George & Hwang (2004); validated for India by Raju (2023), SSRN 4587697
screens.why: The signal is PROXIMITY to the high, not the size of the return that got there. George and Hwang's finding, replicated on Indian equities by Raju over 2004-2023, is that nearness to the 52-week high predicts returns better than academic momentum does, with a higher Sharpe and weaker long-term reversal - the part of momentum that hurts most. The behavioural story is anchoring: the 52-week high is the number everyone remembers, so it acts as a ceiling traders under-react to, and the under-reaction resolves upward.
screens.manage: A ranking signal on a monthly horizon, not a trigger. The research holds it as a portfolio rebalanced periodically, not as an entry with a stop - which is also why it scores poorly in the 1:2 bracket table on this page. The bracket is the wrong instrument for it, and that is a statement about the measurement, not about the effect.
screens.expr: pct_from_52w_high > -12 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and sma_200_slope > 0 and rs_rank >= 80

screens.name: base_breakout_r1
screens.title: Quarter Base, R1 Break
screens.description: A stock that spent the last three months inside a range narrower than twenty-five percent, sitting in the lower half of its fifty-two week range, that has now closed above last month's R1 on volume above its own average.
screens.origin: Weinstein's Stage 1 to Stage 2 transition, triggered on the monthly pivot
screens.why: A long quiet base is where ownership changes hands without a price being paid for it. The people who wanted out after the decline are out, and the range stops widening because nobody left is forced to sell. That is the setup; the pivot break is only the trigger that says the balance has tipped. Requiring the base to sit in the LOWER half of the 52-week range is what separates this from a continuation pattern. A tight range near the highs is a different animal with a different failure mode - this one is buying a turn, not a trend.
screens.manage: Stop under the base's low, which is the level the whole quarter defended. That is usually a long way down, so this is a small-size, wide-stop trade rather than a tight one - and a 3% stop will not survive inside a base that is 25% wide.
screens.expr: base_range_60 < 25 and pct_from_52w_low < 45 and adj_close > m_r1 and since_r1_vol_breakout <= 5 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_200_slope > -3

screens.name: stage2_portfolio
screens.title: Stage 2 Portfolio
screens.description: The Stage 2 base breakout - a close above the highest high of the last sixty sessions on volume, above a rising 30-week average - restricted to breaks that did not gap more than two percent and came from a base no deeper than ten percent. Meant to be held as a basket of up to twenty names for one month and re-run, not as a single trade with a stop.
screens.horizon: Positional - held one month, rebalanced monthly, no stop
screens.origin: Weinstein Stage 2 base breakout, traded as a portfolio rather than a bracket
screens.why: The same signal loses money as a stop-and-target trade and makes money as a monthly portfolio, on the same data. The difference is the exit. The median stock here moves 3.5% on an ordinary day, so any stop inside that range is hit by noise before the thesis resolves; holding twenty names at five percent each and rebalancing on the calendar is the risk control that does not throw the winners away. Of twelve confirmation filters tested on top of the base setup, skipping the gap-up entries was the only one that helped in both time windows and on two different base setups. The others - accumulation, pocket pivots, strong closes, relative strength - either did nothing or cut the sample without adding return.
screens.manage: Run on the first session of each month. Hold the top twenty by the sort, equal weight, for the month. No stop. A name that no longer qualifies at the next rebalance is sold; one that still qualifies is kept. Position size is the risk control: at five percent per name, one halving costs the book 2.5%. Out of sample this beat the equal-weight universe by 2 to 4 percent a month and in 83 to 100 percent of months, over twelve months - a short record, and one measured without costs on a universe that flatters every long strategy.
screens.expr: adj_close > hi_60_prior and adj_close > sma_150 and sma_150_slope > 0 and adj_close > sma_200 and vol_ratio > 1.5 and rs_rank >= 60 and gap_pct <= 2 and base_depth > -10

screens.name: double_seven
screens.title: Double Seven
screens.description: A stock above its 200-day average has just closed below every one of its previous seven closes. The exit is not a target or a stop - it is the mirror image, a close above the previous seven closes.
screens.horizon: Short term - about two weeks, exit on the reversal
screens.origin: Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez, "Short Term Trading Strategies That Work" (2008)
screens.why: Short-term reversal is the best-documented effect at the one-to-two-week horizon, and this is its plainest expression: buy a fresh low inside an uptrend, sell the fresh high that follows. The 200-day filter is what keeps it from catching falling knives, and the reversal exit is what separates it from every bracket on this page - it lets the trade take as long as the reversal takes, rather than cutting it at an arbitrary distance that sits inside one ordinary day's range. On this universe it is the only system that wins by every measure at once: 66% of trades, 80% of months, a profit factor near 1.5, and it does so with no stop at all. Its risk is a position that keeps making new lows; the 20-session time exit is the only protection, and position size the only other one.
screens.manage: Enter at the next open after the signal. Exit at the next open after any close above the prior seven closes, or after twenty sessions. One open position per name. Size small and hold many, because there is no stop. Measured net of 0.3% round-trip costs, out of sample.
screens.expr: new_lo7 == 1 and adj_close > sma_200

screens.name: leader_dip
screens.title: Leader Dip
screens.description: A relative-strength leader (rank 80 or higher against every other stock, price above the 200-day average) that has just closed at a new 7-day closing low, or whose 2-period RSI has dropped below 10. Buy the dip itself, the next open, without waiting for a confirmation candle.
screens.horizon: Short term - about a week, exit on the reversal
screens.origin: Connors' Double Seven and RSI(2), restricted to relative-strength leaders (this project's pullback lab)
screens.why: Of 72 pullback definitions tested on this universe, the two oversold triggers in leaders were the most consistent in both the learning and the holdout period: about two thirds of trades win, roughly +1% per trade net of costs, profit factor near 1.5. Who you buy mattered most (leaders beat all uptrend stocks by 0.5 to 1.0% per trade), buying immediately beat waiting for a reversal bar in every comparison, and the 7-day-high exit beat a fixed hold. The dip definition itself mattered least.
screens.manage: Enter at the next open. Exit at the next open after any close above the prior seven closes, or after twenty sessions. No stop inside the trade; every stop tighter than 15% lowered the return. Size across ten equal slots; a 15% or 3x ATR level is a disaster stop only. One in ten trades loses more than 8%.
screens.expr: rs_rank >= 80 and adj_close > sma_200 and (new_lo7 == 1 or rsi_2 < 10)

screens.name: leader_dip_playbook
screens.title: SW - Leader Dip Playbook
screens.description: The Leader Dip (relative-strength rank 80 or higher, above the 200-day, a new 7-day closing low or RSI(2) under 10) restricted to dips that have NOT broken the 21-day EMA - the close is still at least 2.6 percent above it. A dip that has already lost the 21 EMA is a breakdown, not a pullback. The stop column is the 3 ATR level under the close; place it against the actual fill.
screens.horizon: Short term - about a week and a half, exit on the reversal, hard stop under every trade
screens.origin: This project's synthesis (Sep 2026) - Leader Dip plus the one filter that survived loss forensics
screens.why: Of 78 stock-level and 56 market-level features scored on 35,000 tagged trades, distance above the 21 EMA was the cleanest filter that helped in both halves of the sample: it keeps one signal in five and lifts the win rate from 65 to 73-75 percent in each half, about +2.6 percent per trade net. With a 3 ATR hard stop and ten equal slots the strategy compounded at 48 percent a year with a 7 percent drawdown from June 2024 to September 2026, positive in both halves, and stayed positive under 100 random slot orderings and 20 percent parameter changes. Every tighter stop (3, 5, 8, 10 percent, 2 ATR) lost money in the first half.
screens.manage: Only when the market gate is on - more than half the universe above its 50-day average (off only under 40 percent), or within 126 sessions of a Zweig breadth thrust. Buy the next open. Stop at fill minus 3 ATR(14), placed on fill, never widened, never moved to breakeven. Exit at the next open after any close above the prior seven closes, or at the close of the twentieth session. Ten equal slots, highest RS rank first, one position per stock. Expect roughly three winners in four, an average winner near +6 percent and an average loser near -8 percent; the edge is accuracy, not payoff. STOP MECHANICS (2026 update, from 8-year backtest): the 3/4 ATR stop is checked against the daily CLOSE, not intraday. Wicks below the level do not stop you; only a close below it does, exit next open. This single change lifted the Playbook's CAGR from 21% to 30% at the same drawdown across 2018-2026 by killing false shakeouts, and improves every SW screen tested.
screens.expr: rs_rank >= 80 and adj_close > sma_200 and (new_lo7 == 1 or rsi_2 < 10) and dist_ema_21 >= 2.6

screens.name: trend_stack_swing
screens.title: SW - Trend Stack
screens.description: The FIRST day a stock stacks above its 20, 50 and 200-day averages after at least ten sessions of not doing so - a fresh entry into a Stage 2 stack, not a stock that has sat there for months - taken only when India VIX is in the top third of its one-year range and the Nifty's 20-day high-to-low range is at least 6.9 percent. Those two market conditions mark the first weeks of a rebound after a sell-off; the same entry in a quiet tape is a coin flip. The stop column is three ATRs under the close.
screens.horizon: Swing - two to eight weeks, trailing exit, hard stop under every trade
screens.origin: This project's swing lab (Sep 2026) - a fresh Full Trend Stack, taken only in a volatile tape
screens.why: Across 4,661 fresh trend-stack entries from June 2024 the raw setup won 28 percent of trades with a 3 to 1 payoff. Every stock-level filter failed at least one half of the sample; the two market-level ones here passed both (day-clustered t of 5 in each half), lifting the win rate to 42-44 percent and the average trade to +7.7 percent. As a ten-slot account: 42 percent a year, 5 percent maximum drawdown, positive in both halves and in six of nine quarters, robust to 100 random orderings and to 20 percent parameter changes. The catch is that the filter was on in only three windows of the sample, so treat it as a three-episode result.
screens.manage: Buy the next open. Stop at fill minus 3 ATR(14), placed on fill, never moved. Exit at the next open after any close below the 50-day EMA, or at the close of the 60th session. Ten equal slots, highest RS rank first. Expect to lose six trades in ten and to sit flat for whole quarters when the market filter is off - the winners are +15 to +40 percent trend rides and the losers are one stop each. STOP MECHANICS (2026 update, from 8-year backtest): the 3/4 ATR stop is checked against the daily CLOSE, not intraday. Wicks below the level do not stop you; only a close below it does, exit next open. This single change lifted the Playbook's CAGR from 21% to 30% at the same drawdown across 2018-2026 by killing false shakeouts, and improves every SW screen tested.
screens.expr: fresh_trend_stack == 1 and mkt_vix_pctile_1y >= 63.7 and mkt_nifty_range_20d >= 6.855

screens.name: momentum_swing
screens.title: SW - Momentum Leader
screens.description: The FIRST day a stock qualifies as a Momentum Leader (12-1 momentum over 15 percent, up more than 12 percent in three months and 15 percent in six) after at least ten sessions of not qualifying, while it is within 10 percent of its 52-week high, India VIX is in the top 40 percent of its one-year range, and the breadth gate is on (more than half the universe above its 50-day, or within six months of a breadth thrust). Stop and 1:3 target columns are four and twelve ATRs from the close.
screens.horizon: Swing - two to eight weeks, 1:3 target, hard stop under every trade
screens.origin: This project's swing lab (Sep 2026) - a fresh Momentum Leader near its high, taken only in a volatile tape with the breadth gate on
screens.why: Raw fresh Momentum Leader entries with a 4 ATR stop and a 1:3 target won 46 percent and lost 27 percent of a ten-slot account in the 2025 correction. The three conditions here - near the high, volatile tape, breadth gate - passed both halves of the sample and lifted the win rate to 57 percent with +8 percent per trade: 34 percent a year, 11 percent maximum drawdown, robust to random orderings and parameter changes, but positive in only five of nine quarters and idle in two. Like every trend filter that survived, it is a regime call validated on a handful of rebounds, so size it as a second strategy, not the first.
screens.manage: Buy the next open. Stop at fill minus 4 ATR(14); target at fill plus 12 ATR (three times the risk), both placed on fill; whichever is touched first, the stop wins on a bar that touches both. Time stop at the close of the 60th session. Ten equal slots, highest RS first. Win rate near 57 percent with a 3 to 1 payoff - the losses come in runs when a rebound fails, which is what the breadth gate is there to limit. STOP MECHANICS (2026 update, from 8-year backtest): the 3/4 ATR stop is checked against the daily CLOSE, not intraday. Wicks below the level do not stop you; only a close below it does, exit next open. This single change lifted the Playbook's CAGR from 21% to 30% at the same drawdown across 2018-2026 by killing false shakeouts, and improves every SW screen tested.
screens.expr: fresh_momentum_leaders == 1 and pct_from_52w_high >= -9.94 and mkt_vix_pctile_1y >= 59.9 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: sw_leader_dip_concentrated
screens.title: SW - Leader Dip Concentrated
screens.description: The Leader Dip Playbook (RS rank 80+, above the 200 DMA, at least 2.6 percent above the 21 EMA, breadth gate on) restricted to signals where BOTH short-term triggers fire on the same day: a new 7-day closing low AND an RSI(2) below 10. Fewer trades, deeper dips, higher win rate. Stop column is 3 ATRs below the close, checked against the daily close.
screens.horizon: Swing - about a week and a half, exit on the reversal, hard stop under every trade
screens.origin: The Leader Dip Playbook with both dip triggers required at once (hardening from Sep 2026 8-year backtest)
screens.why: Across 3,050 Playbook signals from 2018-2026 the shipped version wins 69 percent of trades and drops 25 percent from peak in the 2018-19 midcap bear. Requiring BOTH triggers instead of either cuts trades by two-thirds (keeps 24 percent), but wins 72 percent of them at +2.84 percent per trade after costs. As a 10-slot account: 22.5 percent a year, only 14 percent drawdown, worst quarter -7 percent, 23 of 32 quarters positive. The concentrated version is designed for lower activity and lower drawdown — take it when the shipped Playbook has filtered too little for your comfort.
screens.manage: Buy next open. Stop at fill minus 3 ATR(14), checked against the daily close only (wicks below the stop are ignored, exit next open on a close below). Exit next open after any close above the highest close of the previous seven sessions, or at the close of the 20th session. Ten equal slots, highest RS rank first.
screens.expr: rs_rank >= 80 and adj_close > sma_200 and new_lo7 == 1 and rsi_2 < 10 and dist_ema_21 >= 2.6 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: sw_rsi2_snapback
screens.title: SW - RSI(2) Snapback
screens.description: Connors' two-period RSI has dropped under 8 in a stock above both its 50 and 200-day averages, with the 200-day rising and a positive six-month return - a sharp, short pullback inside an established uptrend. Two conditions were added by the swing lab: the close must still be at least 8.7 percent above the 50-day average (the pullback has not reached the trend line), and the market gate must be on (more than half the universe above its 50-day, or within six months of a breadth thrust). Stop column is four ATRs under the close.
screens.horizon: Swing - one to two weeks, exit on the reversal, hard stop under every trade
screens.origin: Connors' RSI(2) pullback, groomed by this project's swing lab (Sep 2026)
screens.why: The raw RSI(2) snapback won 66 percent of trades for +1.0 percent each but lost 30 percent of a ten-slot account in the 2025 correction. Of about 200 filters tested, "still extended above the 50-day" and the breadth gate were the two stock-and-market conditions that raised both win rate and expectancy in each half of the sample. Groomed: 74 percent win, +2.4 percent per trade, profit factor 2.5, only 6 percent of trades stopped, 30 percent a year on ten slots with an 8 percent drawdown, positive in seven of nine quarters (worst -3.2 percent), robust to 100 random orderings and 20 percent parameter changes. It overlaps the Leader Dip Playbook on only 13 percent of trades because it does not require a top-20 RS rank.
screens.manage: Buy the next open. Stop at fill minus 4 ATR(14), placed on fill, never moved. Exit at the next open after any close above the highest close of the previous seven sessions, or at the close of the 60th session. Ten equal slots, highest RS rank first, one position per stock. Roughly 22 signals a month with the gate on; none when it is off. STOP MECHANICS (2026 update, from 8-year backtest): the 3/4 ATR stop is checked against the daily CLOSE, not intraday. Wicks below the level do not stop you; only a close below it does, exit next open. This single change lifted the Playbook's CAGR from 21% to 30% at the same drawdown across 2018-2026 by killing false shakeouts, and improves every SW screen tested.
screens.expr: rsi_2 < 8 and adj_close > sma_200 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_200_slope > 0 and ret_120d > 0 and dist_sma_50 >= 8.7 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: sw_double_seven
screens.title: SW - Double Seven
screens.description: A stock above its 200-day average has closed below every one of its previous seven closes. The swing lab added three conditions: the close is still at least 1 percent above the 21-day EMA (the dip has not broken the short trend), the stock's ATR is at least 5.3 percent of price (a mover, so the bounce is worth the stop), and the market gate is on. It is the Leader Dip's parent rule without the RS-rank requirement; about half its trades are names the Playbook also takes, the rest are high-volatility non-leaders. Stop column is three ATRs under the close.
screens.horizon: Swing - one to two weeks, exit on the reversal, hard stop under every trade
screens.origin: Connors and Alvarez's Double Seven, groomed by this project's swing lab (Sep 2026)
screens.why: Raw Double Seven with a hard stop lost money as an account (-44 percent drawdown, negative first half). With the three filters: 76 percent win, +3.7 percent per trade, profit factor 2.6, 55 percent a year on ten slots with an 8 percent drawdown, both halves strongly positive, six of nine quarters positive (worst -5.0 percent), 5th-percentile of 100 random orderings +51 percent. The high-ATR condition is what turns a sub-1 percent edge into a 3.7 percent one: the same bounce in a 2 percent ATR stock is not worth taking.
screens.manage: Buy the next open. Stop at fill minus 3 ATR(14), placed on fill, never moved. Exit at the next open after any close above the highest close of the previous seven sessions, or at the close of the 60th session. Ten equal slots, highest RS rank first, one position per stock; if a name is already held from the Leader Dip Playbook, do not add. About 21 signals a month with the gate on. STOP MECHANICS (2026 update, from 8-year backtest): the 3/4 ATR stop is checked against the daily CLOSE, not intraday. Wicks below the level do not stop you; only a close below it does, exit next open. This single change lifted the Playbook's CAGR from 21% to 30% at the same drawdown across 2018-2026 by killing false shakeouts, and improves every SW screen tested.
screens.expr: new_lo7 == 1 and adj_close > sma_200 and dist_ema_21 >= 1.0 and atr_pct >= 5.3 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: sw_monthly_r1_retest
screens.title: SW - Monthly R1 Retest
screens.description: Price broke above the monthly R1 pivot two to fifteen sessions ago and has now pulled back to within 1 percent above (or 2.5 percent below) it on the last three days' lows AND today's close is still within 3 percent above R1 (a fresh retest, not a stock that has already run up 5-20 percent away from the level) - broken resistance being tested as support. The swing lab added: the stock is at least 33 percent above its 200-day average (a genuine leader, not a bounce off the bottom), its ATR is at least 4.3 percent of price, and the market gate is on. Stop column is three ATRs under the close.
screens.horizon: Swing - about a week, exit on the reversal, hard stop under every trade
screens.origin: Monthly-pivot R1 retest, groomed by this project's swing lab (Sep 2026)
screens.why: The raw retest with a hard stop won 32 percent on a trailing exit and lost 19 percent a year in the first half. Groomed and switched to the seven-day-high reversal exit: 73 percent win, +1.3 percent per trade, profit factor 1.6, 28 percent a year on ten slots with a 9 percent drawdown, positive in seven of nine quarters (worst -4.1 percent), robust. The edge per trade is the thinnest of the swing screens - six-bar holds, small bounces - but it hardly overlaps the Leader Dip Playbook (about 1 percent of trades on the same day), so it fills slots the other screens leave empty.
screens.manage: Buy the next open. Stop at fill minus 3 ATR(14), placed on fill, never moved. Exit at the next open after any close above the highest close of the previous seven sessions, or at the close of the 60th session. Ten equal slots, highest RS rank first. Treat it as the third choice when the Playbook and Double Seven have nothing: about 28 signals a month with the gate on. STOP MECHANICS (2026 update, from 8-year backtest): the 3/4 ATR stop is checked against the daily CLOSE, not intraday. Wicks below the level do not stop you; only a close below it does, exit next open. This single change lifted the Playbook's CAGR from 21% to 30% at the same drawdown across 2018-2026 by killing false shakeouts, and improves every SW screen tested.
screens.expr: dist_m_r1 > 0 and dist_m_r1 < 3.0 and low3_dist_m_r1 < 1.0 and low3_dist_m_r1 > -2.5 and since_m_r1_cross >= 2 and since_m_r1_cross <= 15 and dist_sma_200 >= 33 and atr_pct >= 4.3 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: vl_volume_spike_breakout
screens.title: VL - Volume Spike Breakout
screens.description: A stock makes a new 20-day CLOSE HIGH on at least 5x its 20-day average volume, closes in the TOP 30 percent of the day's range, has a relative strength rank of at least 60, is above its 200-day SMA, has the 21-EMA above the 50-EMA (short trend above medium trend), and the market gate is on. The stack of filters was chosen because it lifted mean per trade from +1.95 to +4.88 percent and cut drawdown from -18 to -13 percent in both halves of an 8-year sample of 360 trades.
screens.horizon: Swing - 2 to 8 weeks, trailing exit at close < 21 EMA, hard stop
screens.origin: This project's volume lab (Sep 2026) - the filtered winner across 1,920 8-year Midcap trades
screens.why: Volume-spike breakouts on their own win only 39 percent of the time at +2.0 percent per trade and draw down 18 percent. The three additions above raise win rate to 41 percent, double per-trade mean to +4.9 percent, and trim drawdown to -13 percent (equal-weight CAGR + MaxDD score +2.8, the first breakout variant in this study to score positive). Trend continuation, not mean reversion: 40 percent win at 3-to-1 payoff.
screens.manage: Buy next open. Stop is entry minus 3 ATR(14), CHECKED AGAINST THE DAILY CLOSE only (wicks below the stop are ignored - exit next open only if the close settles below). Exit next open after the first close below the 21 EMA, or at the close of session 60. Ten equal slots, highest RS first. Expect roughly one signal a week (45/year), 40 percent win rate with big winners paying for small losers - not a mostly-winning system.
screens.expr: vol_ratio >= 5 and adj_close > close_hi_20 and close_pos >= 0.7 and rs_rank >= 60 and adj_close > sma_200 and ema_21 > ema_50 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: vl_long_base_breakout
screens.title: VL - Long Base Breakout
screens.description: A stock makes a new 2-year (500-session) CLOSE HIGH on at least 2x its 20-day average volume, above its 200-day SMA, with the market gate on. Catches names that have been range-bound or building a long base for years and finally clear the ceiling. These moves, when they succeed, tend to run for months rather than weeks.
screens.horizon: Positional - weeks to months, trailing exit or fixed hold
screens.origin: Multi-year consolidation break (MUKANDLTD-style pattern) - broken resistance turning support
screens.why: Not backtested at scale by this project (multi-year breakouts are rare - perhaps 2-5 per week across the entire universe). Included as a watchlist screen for a pattern that is well-documented in trading literature (O'Neil "cup with handle", Weinstein Stage 2 transition, Minervini "power play"). Trade discretionally with confirmation on the weekly chart; do not size as a system signal.
screens.manage: Add to watchlist on first appearance. Wait for at least 2-3 sessions of holding above the breakout level. Enter at the open of the third close that stays above the level, stop at 3 ATR below entry (close-based), trail behind the 50-day SMA once the trade is +10 percent ahead. This is a positional trade - expect to hold 2-6 months if it works.
screens.expr: adj_close > close_hi_500 and vol_ratio >= 2 and adj_close > sma_200 and mkt_gate_on == 1 and bars_available >= 500

screens.name: vl_wyckoff_spring
screens.title: VL - Wyckoff Spring
screens.description: Today's low undercuts the prior 20-day low (the spring), the close is back above that low (the reclaim), and volume is at least 2x the 20-day average (the effort showing accumulation). Reserved for stocks above their 200-day SMA (spring in a downtrending stock is a failed pattern). Only fires about 40 times a year across the universe - highly selective.
screens.horizon: Short term - 1 to 3 weeks, exit on the reversal, hard stop
screens.origin: Wyckoff Phase C spring - false breakdown that reverses on high volume
screens.why: On 353 signals over 8 years in Nifty Midcap 150 constituents: 70 percent win rate, +1.05 percent per trade net after costs, drawdown -4.1 percent on a 10-slot account. Highest-accuracy volume signal in the lab, but very few trades (~4 per month). Real accumulation only, not a general oversold bounce.
screens.manage: Buy next open. Stop is the spring bar's low minus 0.5 ATR, checked against the daily close (wicks ignored). Exit next open after any close above the highest close of the prior 7 sessions, or at the close of session 20. Size normally (10 percent slot).
screens.expr: spring == 1 and adj_close > sma_200 and vol_ratio >= 2 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: vl_pocket_pivot
screens.title: VL - Pocket Pivot
screens.description: Today is an up day (close greater than previous close), volume exceeds the maximum volume of any DOWN day in the past 10 sessions (accumulation inside a base), the close is above the 50-day SMA, not extended more than 15 percent above the 21-EMA, and above the 200-day SMA. The gate must be on. Buying is showing up inside a consolidation before the breakout does.
screens.horizon: Swing - 2 to 8 weeks, trailing exit at close < 21 EMA
screens.origin: Chris Kacher and Gil Morales - up-day volume beats every down-day volume from the last 10 sessions
screens.why: Classical volume signal, hardened in this project's volume lab. 33 percent win, +1.08 percent per trade net, +10 percent CAGR, -23 percent drawdown across 8 years. Lower win rate than the filtered breakout but fires 5-10x more often, so a natural companion when the market has many stocks basing. Trend continuation - expect payoff-driven, not accuracy-driven, results.
screens.manage: Buy next open. Stop entry minus 3 ATR(14), checked against the daily close. Exit next open after the first close below the 21 EMA, or at the close of session 60. Half slot size (5 percent, not 10) because win rate is one in three; sizing normal risks a losing streak wiping a big chunk of the account.
screens.expr: pocket_pivot == 1 and adj_close > sma_50 and adj_close > sma_200 and dist_ema_21 <= 15 and mkt_gate_on == 1

screens.name: smooth_momentum
screens.title: Smooth Momentum
screens.description: The momentum leaders, restricted to names whose advance came as many small up days rather than a few large ones - at least 55 percent of the last sixty sessions closed higher than the day before.
screens.origin: Da, Gurun and Warachka, "Frog in the Pan" (2014), on top of 12-1 momentum
screens.why: The Frog in the Pan finding is that momentum continues when the path was smooth and reverses when it was jumpy. Gradual information is under-reacted to; a single jump has already been priced. Filtering the momentum portfolio by the share of up days raised its out-of-sample excess return from 1.2 to 2.0 percent a month here, in the direction the paper predicts. A stricter 60 percent cut breaks it - too few names.
screens.manage: A monthly portfolio, not a trade. Top twenty by 12-1 momentum among the names that pass, equal weight, rebalanced on the first session of the month, no stop.
screens.expr: mom_12_1 > 15 and ret_60d > 12 and ret_120d > 15 and adj_close > sma_50 and sma_50 > sma_200 and smooth_60 >= 55
